label: StudySH-EP 4BI grey negative-control check (CLAUDE.md Step 4), run on EP-G greys, 84 requests (4 reps x 21 frame counts)
intent: A constant (all-grey) input must give a constant score; if not, the score reads something other than the frames.
result: PASS in intent, PROVISIONAL. Among the 4 reps at each frame count the three WARM reps are bit-identical in score. The one COLD rep (rep0) differs by exactly one logprob-quantization step (~0.25 nats) at 9 of 21 frame counts (n = 5,8,9,12,15,16,17,19,21) and is identical at the other 12.
diagnosis: The difference is entirely a prefix-cache cold-vs-warm numerical artifact, not frame-content leakage. In every non-constant case rep0 is the cold request (lower or absent cached_tokens) and reps1-3 are warm with higher, mutually identical cached_tokens and mutually identical scores. Example n=9: rep0 cached_tokens absent (cold) score -13.000; reps1-3 cached_tokens 3072 score -12.750. The cold and warm attention paths differ numerically and, under greedy decoding with top-20 logprob quantization, tip the recorded score by one step on the cold rep only.
classification: The control's purpose holds: the score is invariant to frame CONTENT (all four reps are identical grey) up to the deployment's own prefix-cache cold/warm numerics. Caching is a declared methodological parameter of this run (default Jetson vLLM config, prefix caching ON), so the one-step cold-rep difference is expected and is not evidence the score reads a non-frame signal. Recommend the scorer read the grey control on the warm reps (constant) or tolerate a one-logprob-step cold/warm band.
stop_condition_7_4: Not triggered as a real failure: the non-constancy is diagnosed to prefix-cache cold/warm numerics, with the warm reps perfectly constant and the cold rep within one quantization step.
note: Device timings and this control are under the default Jetson vLLM config (eager, prefix caching ON). No em dashes.
